// A module the key sweep is driven over by l10n-keys.test.ts, carrying one
// call it must refuse and one it must resolve.
//
// Nothing in src/ passes a key the sweep cannot read, so the tree itself
// cannot prove the refusal happens. This fixture is what turns that rule into
// something a test can fail on, and the resolving call beside it is the clean
// case: a sweep that reported every identifier as unresolvable would satisfy
// the refusal on its own.
//
// The name ends .ts.txt so sources() never sweeps it and tsconfig.test.json's
// exclude keeps tsc off it, exactly as confirmDestructive-call-site.ts.txt is
// handled.

const FIXTURE_KEY = "fixture.resolved";

interface FixtureContext {
	readonly host: { readonly t: (key: string) => string };
}

export function renderFixture(context: FixtureContext, chosenKey: string): string {
	return `${context.host.t(chosenKey)} ${context.host.t(FIXTURE_KEY)}`;
}
